claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Hf, Mo, and Ta are heavier than candidate substituents Al and Si.
A portion of Hf, Mo, and Ta should be substituted with Al or Si while retaining Ti and Zr.
Substitution with Al or Si will lower the alloy density by 5–10%.
The predicted modified-alloy density is approximately 9.19–9.71 g cm−3.
The proposed substitutions will produce or preserve a BCC solid solution.
Retaining Ti and Zr will help maintain high-temperature strength.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve its room-temperature mechanical properties relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve its elevated-temperature mechanical properties through approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed temperature boundary is room temperature to 1000 °C.
The applicable loading conditions are unspecified.
The substitution amount required to reduce density without sacrificing mechanical properties is uncertain.
Alloys with nominal substitution levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, and 30% should be prepared.
Density, yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation at break should be measured at room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The stated rejection rule requires a density reduction greater than 10% together with failure to maintain or improve mechanical properties.
A yield-strength decrease greater than 10% at room temperature or 1000 °C is offered as an example of mechanical-property failure.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires maintained or improved mechanical properties, but the rejection rule effectively permits decreases of up to 10%. It also requires a density reduction greater than 10% before rejection, whereas the hypothesis targets only a 5–10% reduction, so failure within the target density range would not falsify the stated hypothesis.
